newsitem.title: USA: U.S. dredger charged with negligence in oil slick.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dredger charged with negligence in oil slick.

text.p: A government prosecutor on Friday accused a dredging firm of "gross negligence" in the sinking of the "Smithtown," which leaked hundreds of gallons of oil into New Bedford Harbour during Hurricane Bob in 1991.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jeanne Kempthorne accused Francis Empey, 58, the former owner of Hydro-Dredge Corp., of ignoring the vessel's disrepair and leakage problems. Empey is on trial at a U.S. District Court in Boston charged with violating the Clean Water Act.

"Many, many boat owners in the area adequately prepared (for the August, 1991 hurricane), but Mr. Empey did not," Kempthorne said. He also failed to cooperate in clean-up efforts after the vessel sank, she said.

Empey's lawyer Steven DeYoung said his client did not notice any oil slick in the area where his ship sank immediately after the hurricane. He also said that after the U.S. Coast Guard began cleaning the slick, it became a "federalized project in which (Empey) had no part."
Witnesses testified that in the days after the hurricane, an oil slick spread nearly 2 miles into the harbour at New Bedford, Mass., which is south of Boston.
